fields.name: AnsweredNotAccepted
fields.fieldText:
Understanding the "Find Me" Status: "Answered - Not Accepted". "Answered - Not Accepted" indicates that the call has been forwarded and picked up by the callee, however RingCentral did not recognize that the callee "accepted" the call by pressing "1". Pressing "1" is an option triggerred by enabling the "Incoming call information" feature called "Play announcement before connecting". If RingCentral is not detecting that the callee is pressing "1", this does not always mean that the callee's phone is at fault. Below are some of the common causes that will help identify why RingCentral could not identify that the caller pressed "1" to accept the call.
  • DTMF codes not being recognized
    • There are times that DTMF codes are not being properly passed to RingCentral causing us to "not detect" that the call was already accepted.
    • This can be caused by line quality issues as these codes are passed using distinct tones from one phone system to another. A simple break during the transmission could cause the listening party to not distinguish the code.
  • Call forwarding duration
    • There are instances when the callee is not being given an ample time to press "1" to accept the call.
    • The recommended "Ring for" duration is 20 to 30 seconds, so if the call forwarding rule is below the recommended values, have the customer increase it.
Since the customer answered your test calls but they're experiencing issues, the more call samples provided by this and other customers, the quicker advanced tiers can isolate and resolve the issue.

fields.name: Forcestopped
fields.fieldText:
Understanding the "Find Me" Status: "Force stopped". "Force stopped" is generally the same as "Time out" however it is triggered if there are multiple forwarding numbers involved within the answering rule. It indicates that the system "forces" the call fowarding to "stop" when the set "Ring for" duration was exceeded. This does not always mean that the callee is at fault. Below are some of the common causes that will help identify why the callee did not get the chance to answer the call.
  • Call identifiers
    • Call identifiers may cause problems to the carrier we are forwarding the calls to.
    • There are times that carriers reject the call identifier, generally not letting the call pass through their system.
      • RingCentral may not identify that the call was rejected, causing the call forwarding process to timeout.
  • Post dial delays and call forwarding duration
    • "Time out" happens when the "Ring for" duration has already been met yet RingCentral is still trying to "contact" to the receiving party.
    • The recommended "Ring for" duration is 20 to 30 seconds, so if the call forwarding rule is below the recommended values, ensure that it is increased.
    • Huge delays when call forwarding begins can play a part why callers hangup. The delay happens when RingCentral is routing the call to the forwarding number.
      • Due to the delay, the call forwarding duration may expire while RingCentral is still "connecting" to the forwarding number.
To isolate issues with call identifiers, check if the feature is enabled by going to:
  • "Users" tab
  • Click on "User list" on the left hand panel
  • Click on the extension affected
  • Click on "Call Handling & Forwarding"
  • Click on "Settings"
  • Click "Edit" under "Incoming Call Information"

fields.fieldText:
Identification of the Call Forwarding problem based on unsuccessful test calls. If the customer is still experiencing issues receiving forwarded calls, "Session Log" will tell you why call forwarding is not working.
  • Ask the customer for the phone number where the call came from as well as the date and time of when the call was placed.
  • Search for that call in "Session Log"
  • Note that "Session Log" show all logs in Pacific Time, so if you need help converting the time, please use available online tools such as:
    • Time Difference Calculator
    • Time Zone Converter
Analyzing results from "Session Log" Below are the components to look for when analyzing issues involving call forwarding:
  • Blue: Caller information
    • This indicates the number of the caller. The phone number is under "Caller ID".
    • This component is categorized under "Session Type" as "Caller".
  • Red: Callee information
    • This indicates the number that was dialed as well as the extension which routed the call.
    • This component is also categorized under "Session Type" as "Caller".
  • Orange: DigitalLine information
    • This indicates the DigitalLine number (@sip.ringcentral.com) as well as the user extension the DigitalLine is assigned to.
  • Yellow: "Find Me" status
    • This indicates the number where the call was routed to. The number is under "Called number".
    • The result of the call routing is shown under the column: "Action".
    • This component is categorized under "Session Type": "Find me".
  • Green: Call leg information
    • All calls that show on "Session Log" are grouped into "Legs" shown under "Session ID".
    • Each leg determines what happened during a particular call, from the time the call started, to the time the call ended.
    • "Session ID" is unique for each and every call through RingCentral.

  • The caller's number is 16509184192.
  • The RingCentral number dialed is 13232722313.
  • The user extension the call was routed to, was handled by user extension 555.
  • The call was forwarded to DigitalLine number 13238252222.
  • The DigitalLine number is assigned to user extension 2.
  • The call was successfully answered by the DigitalLine number.

fields.fieldText:
Identify if the forwarding number is blocking any calls.
  • Most carriers allow their users to block certain numbers for various reasons.
  • If the call is blocked, the calling party will get a busy tone.
RingCentral has the ability to send the Caller ID of the RingCentral phone number dialed by the caller.
  • There's a possibility that the forwarding number is set to block calls showing the RingCentral phone number.
Check the User or Extension if Called Number is set to be displayed on forwarded calls. Go to:
  • "Users" tab
  • Click on "User list" on the left hand panel
  • Click on the extension affected
  • Click on "Call Handling & Forwarding"
  • Click on "Settings"
  • Click "Edit" under "Incoming Call Information"

fields.name: LineBusy
fields.fieldText:
Understanding the "Find Me" Status: "Line busy". "Line busy" indicates that the forwarding number cannot be reached by RingCentral because it is "busy". This does not always mean that the forwarding number is at fault. Below are some of the common causes that will help identify why call forwarding is not working.
  • Call identifiers
    • Call identifiers may cause problems to the carrier we are forwarding the calls to.
    • There are times that carriers reject the call identifier, generally not letting the call pass through their system.
  • Outbound routing issues
    • It is possible that the call is not being properly routed to the detination carrier because RingCentral's routing table needs to be updated.
  • Call waiting feature is not active
    • A forwarding number without call waiting will ring "busy" if it is in an active call and another call comes in.
To isolate issues with call identifiers, check if the feature is enabled by going to:
  • "Users" tab
  • Click on "User list" on the left hand panel
  • Click on the extension affected
  • Click on "Call Handling & Forwarding"
  • Click on "Settings"
  • Click "Edit" under "Incoming Call Information"

fields.name: Timeout
fields.fieldText:
Understanding the "Find Me" Status: "Time out". "Time out" generally indicates that the "Ring for" duration was exceeded without the callee answering the phone. This does not always mean that the callee is at fault. Below are some of the common causes that will help identify why the callee did not get the chance to answer the call.
  • Call identifiers
    • Call identifiers may cause problems to the carrier we are forwarding the calls to.
    • There are times that carriers reject the call identifier, generally not letting the call pass through their system.
      • RingCentral may not identify that the call was rejected, causing the call forwarding process to timeout.
  • Post-dial delays and call forwarding duration
    • "Time out" happens when the "Ring for" duration has been exceeded while RingCentral is still trying to "contact" the receiving party.
    • The recommended "Ring for" duration is 20 to 30 seconds.
    • Excessive delays when call forwarding begins can play a part why callers hangup. The delay happens when RingCentral is routing the call to the forwarding number.
      • Due to the delay, the call forwarding duration may expire while RingCentral is still "connecting" to the forwarding number.
To isolate issues with call identifiers, check if the feature is enabled by going to:
  • "Users" tab
  • Click on "User list" on the left hand panel
  • Click on the extension affected
  • Click on "Call Handling & Forwarding"
  • Click on "Settings"
  • Click "Edit" under "Incoming Call Information"

fields.name: UnderstandingthedifferentFindMeStatuses
fields.fieldText:
Understanding the different "Find Me" Statuses "Caller Hangup" generally indicates that the caller hung up before the callee answered the call. "Answered - Not Accepted" indicates that the call has been forwarded and picked up by the callee, however RingCentral did not recognize that the callee "accepted" the call by pressing "1". Pressing "1" is an option triggerred by enabling the "Incoming call information" feature called "Play announcement before connecting". "Call Succeed" indicates that the callee successfully answered the call. "Time out" generally indicates that the "Ring for" duration was exceeded without the callee answering the phone. "Force stopped" is generally the same as "Time out" however it is triggered if there are multiple forwarding numbers involved within the answering rule. It indicates that the system "forces" the call fowarding to "stop" when the set "Ring for" duration was exceeded. Below are some of the network connectivity issues that may cause problems with call forwarding to DigitalLine numbers.
  • Poor internet service directly affects SIP registration and signaling. IP telephony devices configured to connect to RingCentral are registered to RingCentral using an internet connection. Problems with the internet connection should be handled accordingly by the internet service provider.
  • Incorrectly configured network source. A network source that is not configured to work with VOIP will affect SIP registration and signaling. It is best to configure the modem or router to allow connections to and from RingCentral using the ports indicated in this guide: Ports and Firewalls
  • Unsupported IP telephony device. Features that are not working on unsupported devices that were never tested by RingCentral should be referred to their respective manufacturers.
Powercycle the IP telephony device to refresh the Digitalline registration. Wait until the phone re-registers, then have your customer inform the callers to try dialing their number again.

fields.name: UnderstandingtheFindMeStatusLinebusy
fields.fieldText:
Understanding the "Find Me" Status: "Line busy". "Line busy" indicates that the forwarding number cannot be reached by RingCentral because it is "busy". Below are some of the common causes that will help identify why call forwarding is not working.
  • Call waiting feature is not active (only applicable on manually provisioned IP telephony devices)
    • IP telephony devices have the ability to limit the calls they can handle in a given session. Most of the IP phones have configurable web interface in which the call waiting setting can be configured.
      • Polycom phones: "Calls Per Line" is set to "1".
      • Cisco phones: "CW setting" is set to "Disabled".
  • DND status is "enabled"
    • IP telephony devices have a "Do Not Disturb" feature that when enabled, the phone will automatically reject all incoming calls.
    • All calls to the device would ring busy when this feature is turned on.
  • Incorrectly configured network source
    • A network source that is not configured to work with VOIP will affect SIP registration and signaling. It is best to configure the modem or router to allow connections to and from RingCentral using the ports indicated in this guide: Ports and Firewalls.
Powercycle the IP telephony device to refresh the Digitalline registration. Wait until the phone re-registers, then have your customer inform the callers to try dialing their number again.

fields.name: Validatethecallhandlingrules
fields.fieldText:
Validate the call handling rules. If your test call is showing up on "Session Log" but call forwarding is not working, this indicates that the user's answering rule may not be properly configured to forward calls.
  • User hours, after hours, advanced rules, and regional settings
    • Validate the user hours and ensure that the correct forwarding number is configured.
    • Validate any active advanced call handling rule and ensure that they are not conflicting with the customer's call handling rule.
    • If the customer configured both user hours and after hours, ensure that the user is assogned to the regional setting. After hours could be taking effect due the difference in time zones.
Validate the call forwarding rule and ensure that there is no after hours rule or advanced call handling rule that causes the system to not forward calls.

fields.name: VOICEMAILGREETINGS
fields.fieldText:
VOICEMAIL GREETINGS The Voicemail Greeting is what customers hear when they are forwarded to an extension's voicemail during User Hours or After Hours. Callers will hear a default company greeting when they dial your company number. Click Keep Default to keep the default greeting or record a customized by clicking the Custom button.
Set up a Customize Voicemail Greeting You can either Record Over the Phone or Import an audio file. 1. Record Over the Phone
  • Enter your phone number in the Call Me At field and click Call. RingCentral will call you to record your custom greeting over the phone.
  • Your custom greeting will be recorded and activated. Once done recording, click Save then Next
2. Import Audio File
  • Click Browse. Select your audio file.
  • Click Attach
  • Once done, click Save
Click NEXT to review all settings
